comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## The fix direction is DEMONSTRATED, with an honest caveat

Re-ran the same 9 files with a private slot directory — `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)`, so
the run gets its own `locks/` and its own 4 slots — while the four host-global slots stayed
occupied by the other sessions listed in the description:

```
116 passed, 2 errors in 993.46s (0:16:33)
```

**Zero `GateCongestedError`.** Compare the same 9 files minutes earlier against the shared
host slot directory: `14 failed, 102 passed`, every failure `all 4 concurrent slots busy`.
One environment variable is the whole difference, which is as clean a confirmation of the
mechanism as this is going to get.

### The 2 errors are mine, not the suite's

```
ERROR tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py::test_code_change_reruns_full_review
  - Failed: The repo HEAD moved during this test (25d1d683e5 -> 8b2fee219f)
ERROR tests/unit/test_eval_solver.py::test_agentic_case_reroots_injected_runner_at_its_fixture
  - Failed: The repo HEAD moved during this test (8b2fee219f -> 38396ebfcc)
```

Those two SHAs are my own commit and my own `make amend-msg`, run in that worktree while this
verification was still in flight. The suite has a guard for exactly that and it fired
correctly. So: not gate congestion, not a test defect, and not evidence for or against this
ticket — operator error on my part, recorded here rather than quietly dropped, because a
reader comparing "116 passed, 2 errors" against my "zero failures" claim deserves to know
which two and why.

It is also the second time in one session that acting on the tree during a long run polluted
the run. Cheap lesson, stated for the record: do not commit, amend, or edit inside a worktree
that has a suite running in it.

### What this implies for the fix

The change needed is at the FIXTURE level, not in `gate_admission`: point `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`
at a per-session temp dir for the test suite. Production semantics stay exactly as they are —
a real gate op on a real host should contend for a genuinely shared, host-wide semaphore,
which is the whole point of the design. Only the tests need to stop borrowing it.

### Relationship to `torrential-unwhite-snail` (9c2e-b44c-119e-4105)

Read that ticket before assuming this one supersedes it — it does not, and I want the record
straight rather than flattering. 9c2e already frames the cause cross-session ("Any other
session on the machine holding gate slots — another agent running `review-plan` or a
completion-gated close"), and it already asks, in its own AC4, for "a check that no other test
in the suite has the same host-wide coupling, or a ticket filed for any that do".

So this ticket is not a correction of 9c2e. It is the **answer to its AC4**, plus three things
9c2e left open:

1. the concrete code path (`_slot_dir()` -> `store_root()/locks` -> `tempfile.gettempdir()`),
2. the scale (31 tests, 9 files, not 1), and
3. the reason ordinary triage misleads here — admission fails closed WITHOUT waiting, so
   re-running a test alone does not isolate it, and the holders can be processes running no
   tests at all.

If anything is superseded it is the instinct to treat these as one-off flakes; the coupling is
structural and this is its inventory.

comments.body:
CONSOLIDATION — three tickets describe one defect. Naming a canonical so three agents do not solve
it three times.

    846b-4b51-0254-48fd  stuffed-energistic-ladybird   <- CANONICAL
    9c2e-b44c-119e-4105  torrential-unwhite-snail      relates_to (filed first, carries the history)
    bc3e-7f43-2195-4301  dubious-neutral-duck          duplicates (just linked)

All three are the same thing seen from three angles: `gate_admission._slot_dir()` is
`store_root()/locks`, `store_root()` falls back to `tempfile.gettempdir()`, so the four gate
admission slots are **host-global** — shared by every worktree, every session, and every rebar
process on the machine, including ones running no tests at all.

What each contributed, so nothing is lost by consolidating:

- **9c2e** (filed first) recorded the symptom and, in its comments, the xdist-worker angle — four
  `PYTEST_WORKERS` against four slots, with `-n` pinned to the runner's vCPU count (4 on
  ubuntu-latest). That angle is real and is the CI-facing consequence: the gating cell can produce
  a spurious `Verified -1`.
- **846b** established the actual mechanism with the slot-holder table showing all four slots held
  by other sessions' live 15-20 minute LLM gate ops while the observing agent's own pytest count
  was zero — which is why "run it in isolation" does not isolate — plus the fails-closed-without-
  waiting detail and the demonstrated fix (`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` private slot dir: 71 passed / 0
  failed).
- **bc3e** is a third independent sighting from the Windows lock work: 8 of 9 `make verify`
  failures, with `ps` showing another session running `review-plan verminous-zealous-krill`, and an
  A/B proving the change under test was not implicated.

Three independent agents hit this within a few hours, which is itself the strongest argument for
its priority: it is not an occasional flake, it is the default condition on a busy host.

Work the fix on **846b**; leave 9c2e and bc3e open only until it lands, then close them against it.
Do not fix the worker/slot ratio alone — that addresses 9c2e's angle and leaves the host-global
exhaustion untouched, which is the one that makes isolation fail.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Scope note on the private-slot-dir workaround: it is reachable only through the CLI, not through MCP.

Surfaced while an agent was running a plan review under a private `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` to avoid queueing on the shared four-slot semaphore. The workaround works from the CLI and does what it should. It cannot work through the MCP `review_plan` / `review_plan_start` tools, and the reason is structural rather than a bug in the fix: the MCP server is a SEPARATE PROCESS with its own environment, inherited from whatever launched it. An environment variable set in a client's shell — or by an agent about to make a tool call — never reaches that process, so the gate ops it runs resolve their slot directory from the server's environment, not the caller's.

Why this matters here rather than being a footnote. This ticket's remediation direction treats a private slot dir as the escape hatch when the host-global semaphore is contended. That escape hatch is available to exactly the callers least likely to be congesting the host — a local CLI invocation — and unavailable to the MCP surface, which AGENTS.md tells agents to PREFER for long gate ops (`review_plan_start` + poll, precisely because a gate can outlast the client's ~60s deadline). So the guidance steers agents toward the surface where the workaround does not apply.

Not proposing a fix here and not filing a separate bug — this is a property of the remediation's reach, so it belongs on this ticket. Two directions worth weighing when it is picked up: make the slot directory a per-request parameter rather than process-environment state, or have the MCP server resolve it from store/config so it is set where the server can see it. The second keeps it operator-controlled; the first makes it caller-controlled, which is what an agent actually wants mid-congestion.

Recorded from executed evidence, not inference: the CLI run under a private slot dir did proceed while the shared slots were held, which is what makes the asymmetry observable.

Reporting-quality note on this session, since it bears on how findings reach this ticket: the same agent also reported that the gate's suggested `rebar sign-review` remedy "would have papered over a refusal". I checked that against the code and REFUTED it — the message is conditioned on a PASS (`bugfix_size_gate.py:350`), and `resign.py:170-171` states and implements that it never signs a non-PASS/degraded/stale verdict. No bug was filed. Noting it so the refutation is on the record next to the accepted finding, rather than only the accepted half being durable.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
First quantified measurement of what this defect costs, and it is worse than "some gate ops queue": **it corrupts test evidence**.

**Measured 2026-09-05, on an agent's `make verify` run:**

    29 failed, 19751 passed  (41 min)
    26 of the 29 failures: rebar.llm.errors.GateCongestedError
        "gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent slot(s) on this host are in use"

Zero of those failures were in any file the change touched. Re-running the affected gate files SERIALLY: 20 of 21 passed, and the single remaining failure was a different error that passes when its file runs alone.

**So `make verify` — the command AGENTS.md names as "the only local command that lets you say I verified this and be right" — returned red for reasons that had nothing to do with the code under test.** An agent following the documented contract exactly gets a 41-minute run whose verdict is dominated by host contention. The honest agent then cannot say it verified anything; a less careful one would either report a false failure or, worse, start "fixing" tests that were never broken.

That is a different and sharper harm than the one this ticket already records. Queuing wastes wall-clock. This turns the repo's own verification instrument into a source of false negatives, at a rate of 26 failures in one run.

**Cause, and I am the cause.** I am an orchestrating session and I had four agents active on this box at the time, each entitled to gate ops, against a four-slot HOST-GLOBAL semaphore. So my own parallelism saturated the slots and then poisoned my own agents' evidence. Nothing malfunctioned — the semaphore did exactly what it says. The defect is that its scope is the host rather than the workspace, so independent workstreams contend for a resource none of them can see or reason about.

**Two things this sharpens for whoever fixes it.**

First, the failure mode is not merely a refusal: `GateCongestedError` surfaces as a TEST FAILURE, indistinguishable in a summary line from a real one. Whatever the fix, congestion should not be able to render as a red test — an explicit skip, a queue, or a distinguishable error class would all be better than a failure that looks like a defect in the code.

Second, the private-slot-dir workaround recorded above does not help here. An agent running `make verify` is not making a gate call it can wrap in `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`; the gate ops are made deep inside the suite. So the workaround covers the deliberate, single gate op and leaves the suite — where the cost is highest — exposed.

**What I am doing about it in the meantime**, since it is my own concurrency: throttling. I will not add agents while four are active, and I will stagger `make verify` runs rather than letting two agents run them simultaneously. That is mitigation by discipline, not a fix, and it is only available to a session that knows the defect exists.

compiled_state.description:
## What was observed

A full `make verify` on 2026-09-04 in worktree `bug-9c93-ad8d-user-data-mounts` (a
`user_data.sh` mount-assertion change, zero overlap with the LLM gate path) reported:

```
31 failed, 19489 passed, 75 skipped, 14 warnings in 4131.23s (1:08:51)
```

28 of the 31 were `rebar.llm.errors.GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4
concurrent slots busy`. The other 3 (`tests/unit/test_plan_review_cli_retry.py`,
`assert 11 == 2` on an LLM call count) were knock-on and passed in isolation.

**Re-running the 9 affected files ALONE still produced 14 failures.** That is the finding:
"run it alone" does not isolate this, so the usual triage step gives a FALSE "this is real
and it is mine" verdict.

## The mechanism

`rebar.llm.gate_admission._slot_dir()` returns `store_root() / "locks"`, and
`rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot.store_root()` resolves to `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` **or else
`tempfile.gettempdir()`**. On a developer box with `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` unset that is a single
directory shared by **every worktree, every session and every process on the machine**. The
four `gate-slot-N` files in it are therefore a HOST-GLOBAL semaphore, not a per-suite or
per-worktree one.

Two consequences:

1. The slots can be exhausted by processes that are **running no tests at all**.
2. Admission **fails closed WITHOUT waiting** — `_acquire_slot` returns `None` and the caller
   raises immediately (`gate_admission.py:305`, ":class:`GateCongestedError` without waiting
   when every slot is taken"). So a test needing a slot dies instantly rather than queueing
   behind the holder. Serialising the test run does not help; only freeing a slot does.

## Proof: who actually held the slots

Taken live with `lsof` on the four slot files while my own pytest count was **zero**:

| slot | PID | holder cwd | process |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gate-slot-0` | 50765 | `/Users/joeoakhart/janitor-e54e-shims` | `rebar verify-completion` |
| `gate-slot-1` | 6229 | `/Users/joeoakhart/janitor-f773-cli` | `rebar review-plan` |
| `gate-slot-2` | 20256 | `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar` | global `rebar-dev` release build |
| `gate-slot-3` | 89566 | `/Users/joeoakhart/janitor-038d-config` | `rebar` gate op |

All four were **other sessions' real 15-20 minute LLM gate operations**, in four different
worktrees. None was a test. None was mine. That is why the failures survived isolation, and
it is the part that a "concurrent xdist workers exhaust the suite's own slots" framing does
not predict: the exhausting processes need not be running the suite, or any suite.

## Scope: 31 tests across 9 files

This is not one test. Observed failing under contention:

- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_retry.py` (16)
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py` (6 under isolation; 1 in the full run)
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_cli_retry.py` (3, knock-on `assert 11 == 2`)
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_producer_seam_8d8e.py` (2)
- `tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py` (2)
- `tests/unit/test_gate_peak_rss_9ea3.py` (2)
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar_heldout.py` (2)
- `tests/unit/test_eval_solver.py` (1)
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar.py` (1)

This directly answers AC4 of `torrential-unwhite-snail` (`9c2e-b44c-119e-4105`), which asked
for "a check that no other test in the suite has the same host-wide coupling, or a ticket
filed for any that do". They do; this is that ticket.

## CI consequence

These tests are red whenever four real gate ops are in flight anywhere on the same machine —
**including in CI if a runner is ever shared, or if a self-hosted runner also hosts gate
work**. The failure names gate congestion, so it reads as an infrastructure problem rather
than a test defect, which is exactly the shape that gets `recheck`ed instead of fixed. Per
AGENTS.md that makes it a bug to root-cause, not a retry candidate: it is reproducible by
construction (occupy all four slots, run the tests), not random.

## Proposed fix direction

Give the test suite its **own** slot directory rather than the host's, by pointing
`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` at a per-session temp dir in the test fixture. That is a one-line
environment change at the fixture level and needs no change to `gate_admission`'s logic, so
it keeps the production semantics (a genuinely shared host semaphore) exactly as they are
while removing the cross-session coupling from the tests.

**Not implemented here deliberately.** It touches the gate-admission path that several agent
sessions are exercising concurrently right now, and the change that surfaced it was about
`user_data.sh` mounts. Keeping them separate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 - The coupling is reproduced deterministically: occupy all 4 host slots from a
      process that runs no tests, then run the 9 files above and observe the same failures.
      This must be a real reproduction, not an assumption from the field evidence.
- [x] AC2 - The listed tests pass with all four HOST slots held by an unrelated process.
- [x] AC3 - What each test actually asserts is still asserted. The fix must not be skipping,
      deleting, or `xfail`ing them, and must not weaken gate admission itself.
- [x] AC4 - Production semantics are unchanged: a real gate op on a real host still contends
      for a shared, host-wide semaphore. The isolation applies to the TEST suite only.
- [x] AC5 - Some guard stops a future test re-acquiring the host-global slot silently, so the
      class does not simply grow back.
compiled_state.title: Gate admission's 4 slots are HOST-GLOBAL (store_root()/locks under tempfile.gettempdir()), so ~31 unit tests across 9 files go red whenever any process on the box holds a real gate op
